label: Late copy phase: outputting original token 4 or later
explanation: Positional copy-phase feature. Fires on copy-phase steps once the model is recalling original position 4 or beyond (recall_idx >= 4); essentially 0 during original input, at <DEL>, and for recall_idx 0-3. Rate is ~50% at recall_idx 4 (higher for short L=5-6, lower for long sequences, where it often starts one step later) and ~98-100% for recall_idx >= 5. Activation ramps up step by step through the copy phase, peaking at the final output steps (top examples are the last 1-2 outputs of L=8-9 sequences). Not token-specific: in_tok, out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok and next_out all show flat lift. Misses are weak onset activations at recall_idx 3; false positives are mostly recall_idx 4 in longer sequences. Adding (recall_idx>=5 | L<=6) raises dev F1 from 0.90 to 0.93 but the simpler predicate already captures 99.7% of the mass.

issues: One claim in the explanation is wrong. It says missed activations are 'weak onset activations at recall_idx 3', but recall_idx==3 has only 25 active steps out of 486,935 on dev (precision 5e-5). The roughly 11k missed steps are almost all tiny (about 0.09 of max) activations in the original phase at t=1 (8,724), t=2 (1,691) and t=5 (320), for example 'a [e:0.09] a u <DEL>'. They hold only 0.3% of the activation mass, so this does not affect the label.

The recall_idx==4 onset depends strongly on L. Test precision at recall_idx 4 is 0.76 for L=5, 0.79 for L=6, 0.51 for L=7, 0.29 for L=8 and 0.15 for L=9. So '~50%' is only the pooled rate. It matches the stated direction (higher for short sequences), and almost all false positives come from this boundary.

I found no token or history variable that explains which recall_idx-4 steps fire when L>=7. Rates conditioned on in_count, out_count, n_digits or digit in_tok/out_tok all stay between 0.29 and 0.39, so the boundary is a graded threshold, not a hidden token rule. The flat-lift claim holds.

Magnitude does not always peak at the final step. Some mid-quartile examples dip at the end (e.g. 'q i z k w i r p n': 0.57 -> 0.45 -> 0.44; 'g z r k d b 3 0 m': 0.65 -> 0.52). The top examples do peak at the last 1-2 outputs of L=8-9 sequences, and to_go==0 holds 41% of the activation mass, so the claim holds in the aggregate.
The test scores reproduce: P=0.828, R=0.989, F1=0.901, mass recall 0.997. The refined predicate reaches test F1 0.934 (P 0.955, R 0.914), but its mass recall drops to 0.962.
